# Changelog

## [1.1.0] - 2026-10-07

### New Features

- **Program status reporting**: terminals and agent dashboards that support OSC 7501 see whether Pi is working, blocked on a dialog or login, done, or failed. See [Program status](docs/terminal-setup.md#program-status).
- **Claude Haiku 5.5**: `anthropic/claude-haiku-5-5`, with adaptive thinking up to `xhigh`/`max` effort.
- **Adjust default tools with `+name`/`-name`**: `--tools` entries like `pi -t +codemode,-write` change the default selection instead of replacing it. See [Tools](docs/cli.md#tools).
- **GPT-6 Luna and image classification**: OpenAI's GPT-6 Luna is available as a classifier model through the Decisions API, and codemode's `models.classify()` accepts images for classifiers that support them. See [Use classifier models](docs/models.md#use-classifier-models).
- **Native llama.cpp decision models**: Julia-1, Laya, Kev, lev, and OpenJev served by llama.cpp 0.6.0 or later run natively as classifiers through `/v1/systemone`. See [Classification](docs/llama-cpp.md#classification).

### Added

- Added `+name` and `-name` entries to `--tools`, which change the default tool selection instead of replacing it, for example `pi -t +codemode`
- Added `durationMs` to the tool render context and to `tool_execution_end` extension events: the recorded execution time of a final tool result ([#10549](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10549))
- Added `outputPad` to the tool render context ([#10557](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/10557) by [@rwachtler](https://github.com/rwachtler))
- Added OpenAI's GPT-6 Luna as a classifier model through the Decisions API, available with `OPENAI_API_KEY` (see [Use classifier models](docs/models.md#use-classifier-models))
- Added `images` to codemode's `models.classify()` context, so classifiers that accept images, such as GPT-6 Luna, can judge them
- Added program status reporting with OSC 7501: terminals and agent dashboards that support it see whether Pi is working, blocked on a dialog or login, done, or failed. `PI_PROGRAM_STATUS=1|0` overrides detection (see [Terminal setup](docs/terminal-setup.md#program-status)) ([#10607](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10607))
- Added `aborted` to `agent_settled` session, extension, and JSON events, so integrations can tell a cancelled run from a finished one ([#10607](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10607))
- Added Claude Haiku 5.5 (`anthropic/claude-haiku-5-5`), with adaptive thinking up to `xhigh`/`max` effort and prompt caching on Bedrock
- Added native llama.cpp decision models: Julia-1, Laya, Kev, lev, and OpenJev served by llama.cpp 0.6.0 or later are listed only as classifiers through `/v1/systemone` instead of as chat models (see [Classification](docs/llama-cpp.md#classification)) ([#10382](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/10382))

### Changed

- Changed `outputPad` to also apply to `!` command output, tool output, and summary blocks ([#9946](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/9946), [#10557](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/10557) by [@rwachtler](https://github.com/rwachtler))
- Changed `pi mcp login --timeout` to limit the whole sign-in, including requests to the authorization server, instead of only the wait for the browser ([#10565](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10565))

### Fixed

- Fixed bash and PowerShell results losing `Took` after reloading a session, and the live `Took` including wall-clock steps; both now show the recorded execution time ([#10549](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10549))
- Fixed managed installs keeping every old release; `pi update` now keeps only the new release and the one it updated from ([#10392](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10392), [#10511](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/10511) by [@davidbrai](https://github.com/davidbrai))
- Fixed standalone binaries loading `.env`, `.env.local`, and `.env.development` from the launch directory into Pi's environment ([#10473](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10473))
- Fixed `!!` command headers losing their dim color once output arrives ([#10557](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/10557) by [@rwachtler](https://github.com/rwachtler))
- Fixed the codemode description not marking `searchTools()`, `describeTool()`, and `describeNamespace()` as async, which led models to serialize the unawaited promise as `{}` ([#10555](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10555))
- Fixed codemode output items running together, so models could not tell where one `text()` or `console.log()` output ended and the next began. With several text items, each now starts with a `==> text N/M <==` line, and `console` calls follow the other output in one `<console_output>` block with one line per call
- Fixed `/mcp` waiting for all servers to connect before opening; the manager now updates live and remains usable while enabling, reconnecting, or disabling servers ([#10562](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10562))
- Fixed images being dropped as "could not be resized" when running under `node --watch` on Node 24.19+ and 26.x, where Node posts its own messages on the image resize worker channel ([#10527](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10527))
- Fixed clipboard paste doing nothing in Termux, and failed copies there omitting the Termux:API install hint ([#10391](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10391))
- Fixed `!` and RPC `bash` output keeping fragments of color codes, such as a stray `m`, when a code was split across output chunks ([#10504](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10504))
- Fixed MCP OAuth sign-ins that could not be cancelled while waiting on the authorization server and kept running after the session ended. The sign-in screen now cancels with Esc at every step, session shutdown aborts a running sign-in, and each request to the authorization server times out after 15 seconds ([#10565](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10565))
- Fixed shutdown waiting up to 15 seconds to refresh an MCP OAuth token that was about to expire, only to close the server's session ([#10565](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10565))
- Fixed the fullscreen text selection surviving session switches and other transcript rebuilds, which highlighted unrelated text in the new transcript ([#9311](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/9311), [#10567](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/10567) by [@christianklotz](https://github.com/christianklotz))
- Fixed OpenAI models on Bedrock ignoring the thinking level and always running at Bedrock's default reasoning effort ([#9331](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/9331), [#10142](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/10142) by [@jsanter27](https://github.com/jsanter27))
- Fixed model `headers` in `models.json` not overriding the `originator` and `User-Agent` headers of Codex requests ([#10429](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/10429) by [@lucasmeijer](https://github.com/lucasmeijer))
- Fixed `server_busy` and `servers are currently busy` provider errors ending the turn instead of being retried ([#10543](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10543))
- Fixed Mistral responses that end with `finish_reason: "error"` not being retried ([#10487](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10487))
- Reduced context-limit request failures by estimating input at 3.5 characters per token instead of 4 when calculating output limits ([#10497](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10497))
- Fixed Radius models disabled by an organization owner still being listed
- Fixed Anthropic browser login failing with "localhost refused to connect" when port 53692 is reserved or in use, for example by Hyper-V/WSL port exclusions on Windows: login now falls back to a free loopback port ([#10571](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10571))
- Fixed session costs undercounting long prompts on models with prompt-length pricing tiers, such as Claude Haiku 5.5, Gemini 3.1 Pro, and GPT-5.4, through OpenCode, OpenCode Go, OpenRouter, Vercel AI Gateway, Google, MiniMax, and other providers
- Fixed Markdown links not being clickable in Herdr ([#10573](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10573))

## [1.0.4] - 2026-10-05

### New Features

- **Tool patterns and `--no-mcp`**: `--tools` and `--exclude-tools` accept `*` patterns, for example `--tools read,codemode,'mcp__radius__*'` keeps only one MCP server's tools. `--tools` now keeps MCP tools unless an entry starts with `mcp__`, and `--no-mcp` turns off MCP for one run. See [Tools](docs/cli.md#tools) and [MCP tools](docs/cli.md#mcp-tools).
- **Codemode persists images**: `tools.read()` on an image file now gives back an image block that `image()` can show. See [Call tools](docs/codemode.md#call-tools).

### Added

- Added `*` patterns to `--tools` and `--exclude-tools`, for example `--tools read,codemode,'mcp__radius__*'`
- Added `--no-mcp` to disable the built-in MCP support for one run

### Fixed

- Fixed syntax highlighting losing colors after the first line of multiline strings and comments in fenced code blocks ([#10143](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10143))
- Fixed codemode scripts not receiving images from `read`: `tools.read()` now resolves to an image block for image files, which `image()` shows ([#10251](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10251))
- Fixed MCP OAuth sign-in failing with `invalid_redirect_uri` on servers with OpenID Connect client registration, such as `mcp.modem.dev`: pi now registers as a native client ([#10493](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10493))
- Fixed `--tools` removing MCP tools, which left `pi --tools codemode` without any MCP servers. `--tools` now keeps MCP tools unless an entry starts with `mcp__`
- Fixed MCP session shutdown returning while a server was still connecting, leaving its transport open until the server answered or timed out ([#10249](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10249))
- Fixed system prompt rules and the skills hint naming tools hidden by `prepareLoadout`. Hidden tools are left out of the rules, the skills hint names no tool when the file reader is hidden, and `codemode` shows each tool's prompt guidelines with its declaration; `ToolLoadout` gains `getPromptGuidelines()` ([#10343](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10343))
- Fixed Bedrock requests that fail with `The pending stream has been canceled` after a stalled HTTP/2 connection not being retried automatically ([#10379](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10379))
- Fixed codemode scripts that patch built-ins (for example `Array.prototype.toJSON = ...`) crashing pi and leaving the tool call unsettled. Built-ins are now frozen before the script runs, so such patches have no effect ([#10444](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10444))

# RPC Extension UI

Extensions can request user interaction through `ctx.ui`. In RPC mode, supported calls become a request/response subprotocol alongside normal [RPC commands](rpc-commands.md) and [session events](json.md).

There are two categories of extension UI methods:

- **Dialog methods** (`select`, `confirm`, `input`, `editor`): emit an `extension_ui_request` on stdout and block until the client sends back an `extension_ui_response` on stdin with the matching `id`.
- **Fire-and-forget methods** (`notify`, `setStatus`, `setWidget`, `setTitle`, `set_editor_text`): emit an `extension_ui_request` on stdout but do not expect a response. The client can display the information or ignore it.

If a dialog method includes a `timeout` field, the agent-side will auto-resolve with a default value when the timeout expires. The client does not need to track timeouts.

## Limitations

Some `ExtensionUIContext` methods are not supported or degraded in RPC mode because they require direct terminal UI access:

- `custom()` returns `undefined`.
- `onTerminalInput()` returns a no-op unsubscribe function.
- `setWorkingMessage()`, `setWorkingVisible()`, `setWorkingIndicator()`, `setHiddenThinkingLabel()`, `setFooter()`, `setHeader()`, `addAutocompleteProvider()`, `setEditorComponent()`, and `setToolsExpanded()` are no-ops.
- `getEditorText()` returns `""` and `getEditorComponent()` returns `undefined`.
- `getToolsExpanded()` returns `false`.
- `pasteToEditor()` delegates to `setEditorText()` without terminal paste handling.
- `getAllThemes()` returns `[]`, and `getTheme()` returns `undefined`.
- `setTheme()` returns `{ success: false, error: "Theme switching not supported in RPC mode" }`.

Note: `ctx.mode` is `"rpc"` and `ctx.hasUI` is `true` in RPC mode because the dialog and fire-and-forget methods are functional via the extension UI sub-protocol. Use `ctx.mode === "tui"` to guard TUI-specific features like `custom()` that require a real terminal.

## Requests from Pi

All requests have `type: "extension_ui_request"`, a unique `id`, and a `method` field.

### confirm

Prompt the user for yes/no confirmation.

```json
{
  "type": "extension_ui_request",
  "id": "uuid-2",
  "method": "confirm",
  "title": "Clear session?",
  "message": "All messages will be lost.",
  "timeout": 5000
}
```

Expected response: `extension_ui_response` with `confirmed: true/false` or `cancelled: true`.

----program status
## Program status

Pi reports its state with the [Program Status Protocol (OSC 7501)](https://www.superlogical.com/rex/docs/build/program-status), so terminals and agent dashboards can show whether it is working, waiting for you, done, or failed:

| State | When |
|---|---|
| `working` | An agent run or compaction is in progress. The message is the session name. |
| `blocked` | An extension dialog or login waits for you. The message is the dialog title. |
| `done` | A run finished. The message is the session name. |
| `error` | A run ended with an error that is not retried. The message is the first line of the error. |
| `idle` | Pi started, or you cancelled the run. |

Reports never contain prompts or model output. Pi sends them only after the terminal answers the protocol's support query; tmux and screen do not forward them. Set `PI_PROGRAM_STATUS=1` to send reports without asking, or `PI_PROGRAM_STATUS=0` to turn them off.

## Start RPC mode

```bash
pi --mode rpc --no-session
```

Normal CLI options still select the working folder, model, tools, resources, and session behavior. Common choices include `--provider`, `--model`, `--name`, `--no-session`, and `--session-dir`. See [Command Line](cli.md) for the complete, version-specific interface; `pi --help` is authoritative for the installed version.

RPC mode rejects `@file` prompt arguments. Send prompts through the [`prompt`](rpc-commands.md#prompt) command instead.

## Protocol records
## Minimal client

This Python example uses a binary pipe reader, which splits on LF without treating Unicode separators as protocol boundaries:

```python
import json
import subprocess

process = subprocess.Popen(
    ["pi", "--mode", "rpc", "--no-session"],
    stdin=subprocess.PIPE,
    stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
)

assert process.stdin is not None
assert process.stdout is not None

command = {"id": "prompt-1", "type": "prompt", "message": "Hello"}
process.stdin.write(json.dumps(command).encode("utf-8") + b"\n")
process.stdin.flush()

while line := process.stdout.readline():
    record = json.loads(line)
    if record.get("type") == "message_update":
        update = record["assistantMessageEvent"]
        if update["type"] == "text_delta":
            print(update["delta"], end="", flush=True)
    elif record.get("type") == "agent_settled":
        print()
        break

process.stdin.close()
process.wait()
```

For maintained TypeScript clients, use the checked [RPC client example](../examples/rpc-client.ts). It requires a built Pi CLI because the repository example points to `dist/cli.js`.

# PRD-010 / #152: integrated research-cycle feasibility

## Scope and evidence

Source: [issue #152](https://github.com/feniix/pi-extensions/issues/152) and
[PRD-010](../prd/PRD-010-pi-exa-integrated-research-cycle.md).
This is feasibility/design work, not the integrated-cycle implementation.
No live Exa calls were made. One operator-requested TypeSafe design-selection
request used Jev; it is not a proposed runtime dependency.

Verified baseline: committed lockfile, pnpm 12.8.1, `exa-js` 2.23.0,
Pi 1.0.3, bridgekit 0.15.0. The initial local Pi installation was 0.86.1;
`pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` restored the graph without changing dependencies.
Distinguish documented remote capabilities, observed installed/offline behavior,
proposed contracts, and unverified runtime/account guarantees.

## Agent capability matrix

| Capability | Evidence and limits |
|---|---|
| Structured output | Documented `outputSchema` / `output.structured`; SDK forwards schema and retains data. SDK typing does not validate schemas or prove evidence. |
| Grounding | Documented optional field-level citations; SDK preserves them. Local formatter flattens citations; future envelope must retain associations. |
| Input records | `input.data` means processing/enrichment rows, not evidence attachments. `input.exclusion` excludes returned entities, not reading or security filtering. |
| Selected evidence | No dedicated source-pack field established. Use labeled query context, not processing rows. Source fidelity remains unverified. |
| Continuation | Completed same-team `previousRunId` creates a new run; not polling, recovery, or idempotency. ZDR cannot assume continuation support. |
----
# npm to pnpm migration fact-check

Research date: 2026-09-30 UTC (2026-09-29 locally).
Repository baseline: `6586e7bed90c1eef8c3c583674779cd704809048`.

## Conclusion and evidence boundary

Migration is feasible in principle, but clean-install and runtime compatibility
remain untested. Repository inspection and primary-source research were followed
by an independent evidence audit. No dependency installation, migration, functional
test suite, audit, packing, workflow dispatch, or publication was performed.

# PRD-010 / #171: Pi host capabilities for guided background research

Research date: 2026-10-12 UTC. Target host: Pi 1.1.0 (`@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent`,
the latest 1.x at the time; the workspace pin moved from 1.0.3 in this slice).
Exa SDK: `exa-js` 2.23.0 (unchanged). Source: issue #171, PRD-010 v1.3 and the
[architecture contract](../architecture/plan-pi-exa-integrated-research-cycle.md).

## Scope and evidence boundary

This document records what the pinned Pi host can and cannot guarantee for the
6.1.0 journey: request → clarify → preview scope/cost → trusted approval →
submit → return the research ID and control → background monitoring →
completion notification → report. Evidence comes from three sources, each
labeled below:

- **Docs**: the shipped `docs/*.md` and `dist/**/*.d.ts` of Pi 1.1.0.
- **Source**: the shipped `dist/core/agent-session.js`, `dist/core/extensions/runner.js`
  and `dist/modes/rpc/rpc-mode.js` of Pi 1.1.0 (line references are to that build).
- **Experiment**: the runnable prototype in
  `packages/pi-exa/__tests__/fixtures/guided-prototype/` driven by
  `packages/pi-exa/__tests__/guided-prototype.test.ts` (in-process SDK session,
  scripted model) and `packages/pi-exa/__tests__/guided-prototype.rpc.test.ts`
  (a real `pi --mode rpc` child process). Both use a controllable mocked Exa job.

No paid Exa call, live model call, interactive TUI smoke or publication was
performed. The prototype is design evidence; it does not implement PRD-010 and
does not touch the merged v1.2 foundation. An interactive TUI demonstration is the
#175 gate.

## Capability matrix

| Requirement | Pi 1.1.0 capability | Evidence | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| Trusted operator approval in the normal guided flow | `ctx.ui.confirm(title, message, { timeout, signal })` is available to tool `execute()` through `ExtensionToolContext`; it blocks the tool until the dialog resolves. Only extension code that received a `true` result can write a grant; no tool parameter can carry one. | Docs `extensions/types.d.ts` (`ExtensionUIContext.confirm`, `ExtensionUIDialogOptions`); Experiment: SDK test "approves through the trusted dialog" and RPC test (dialog title/body carried the proposal, `timeout: 600000`). | Supported |
| Confirmation in RPC/headless clients | RPC forwards `confirm` as `extension_ui_request` and resolves `false` on `cancelled: true` or timeout; `ctx.hasUI` is `true` in TUI and RPC. Print/JSON modes bind no UI: `hasUI` is `false` and the default `confirm` resolves `false`. | Source `runner.js` (`noOpUIContext.confirm: async () => false`; `hasUI()` is `uiContext !== noOpUIContext`), `rpc-mode.js:85`; Docs `rpc-extension-ui.md`; Experiment: SDK test "fails closed without a trusted confirmation surface" (`hasUI=false`, `APPROVAL_UNAVAILABLE`, zero creates), RPC test cancelled dialog → `APPROVAL_NOT_GRANTED`. | Supported; fail closed on `hasUI === false` before calling `confirm`, because a silent `false` is indistinguishable from a decline |
| Distinguish decline, dismissal and timeout | `confirm` returns a bare boolean. The extension cannot tell a decline from a timeout or a cancelled dialog. | Docs `ExtensionUIContext.confirm(): Promise<boolean>`. | Unsupported; report "not granted" and never infer consent |
| Tool returns while the remote job is pending | A tool `execute()` may return after the create acknowledgement; later work continues on extension-owned timers. `pi.sendMessage` is usable from a timer callback (no `ctx` needed). | Experiment: SDK and RPC tests show the tool result "Research started: run_1 … status running" while the mock job stays `running`, followed by an intervening user prompt. | Supported |
| Background scheduling while Pi runs | Node timers started from a tool or `session_start` and cleared in `session_shutdown`. Pi forbids starting timers in the extension factory. | Docs `extensions.md` "Respect the runtime lifecycle"; Experiment: monitor timers in the prototype. | Supported (in-process only; nothing runs after Pi exits) |
| Safe-turn assistant wakeup | `pi.sendMessage(message, { triggerTurn: true, deliverAs: "followUp" })`: idle → appends the custom message and starts a turn now; streaming → queues it after pending work; during `agent_settled` emission → deferred until settlement completes. `deliverAs: "steer"` would enter after the current assistant turn instead. | Source `agent-session.js` `sendCustomMessage` (lines ~1770–1800, `_isEmittingAgentSettled`, `_deferredSettledActions`); Experiment: SDK test "queues a completion that lands during an active response" shows the notice appended after the streaming assistant message, then the report turn. | Supported |
| Safe boundary signal for extensions | `agent_settled` (now with `aborted`) is the final notification-only boundary; `agent_before_settle` and `turn_end` are actionable. `ctx.isIdle()` and `ctx.hasPendingMessages()` exist but timers have no `ctx`; relying on Pi's queue is sufficient. | Docs `extensions.md`; Pi 1.1.0 changelog (`aborted` on `agent_settled`); Experiment: `agent_settled:aborted=true` observed after `session.abort()`. | Supported |
| Delivery acknowledgement | `pi.sendMessage` returns `void`; rejections are reported as extension errors, not to the caller. There is no API-level acknowledgement. Pi appends a `custom_message` entry to the session file when it actually delivers; an extension can observe that entry (with its own `details`) through `ctx.sessionManager.getEntries()` on `agent_settled` or `session_start`. | Source `agent-session.js` `runner.bindCore({ sendMessage: … .catch(emitError) })`, `_appendCustomMessage`; Docs `session-format.md` (`custom_message` entries); Experiment: `notice_acknowledged` after locating the entry; RPC `get_entries` shows `custom_message:exa-proto-completion`. | Partially supported: acknowledgement by observation, not by return value |
| Durability of queued deliveries | Streaming-time queues (`steer`, `followUp`, `nextTurn`, deferred custom messages) live in process memory until Pi appends them. A crash between `sendMessage` and the append loses the host copy; only the extension's own pending record survives. | Source `agent-session.js` `_pendingCustomMessages`, `_pendingNextTurnMessages`, `agent.followUp/steer`. | Unsupported exactly-once; keep a durable pending notice and reconcile |
| Origin-session targeting | One extension runtime serves one session. `ctx.sessionManager.getSessionId()` identifies it at `session_start`. There is no API to deliver into another session. Session replacement (new/resume/fork/switch) emits `session_shutdown` and invalidates the old runtime; later use of the old `pi` throws the stale-context error. SDK `session.dispose()` invalidates without emitting `session_shutdown`. | Source `agent-session.js` `dispose()` → `runner.invalidate(...)`, `runner.js` `invalidate`; Experiment: SDK test "fences delivery after the runtime is invalidated" (`notice_delivery_failed`, `deliveryError` contains "stale", a second session with a different ID discovers but does not deliver the foreign notice); RPC test `new_session` → monitor `paused:SHUTDOWN`. | Supported for same-session delivery; cross-session delivery unsupported by design |
| Discoverability after restart | `session_start` carries `reason: startup | reload | new | resume | fork` and a `ctx` with the session ID; durable state outside the session must be read by the extension. Nothing resumes implicitly. | Docs `SessionStartEvent`; Experiment: pending notices reported with origin/foreign classification; previous runtime monitors marked `paused:RESTART`. | Supported |
| Blocked-on-dialog visibility | Pi 1.1.0 reports `blocked` with the dialog title through OSC 7501 to supporting terminals and emits `ui_prompt_start/end` extension events. | Docs `terminal-setup.md` "Program status"; `extensions/types.d.ts` `UIPromptStartEvent`. | Supported (informational) |
| Server retry guidance for GET backoff | `ExaError` exposes `statusCode`, `type`, `code`, `detail`; no `Retry-After` value is surfaced by the pinned SDK. | Docs `exa-js` `dist/index.d.ts` `class ExaError`. | Unsupported; use local backoff |
| Create abort / server idempotency | Not assumed. The prototype never cancels and the SDK create is not aborted; an unacknowledged create stays `unknown` and a late acknowledgement settles the original attempt. | Experiment: SDK test "keeps an unacknowledged create unknown and saves a genuine late run ID without resubmitting" (`late_ack`, one create). | Unsupported by design; fail closed |

## Experiment summary

The SDK test (`guided-prototype.test.ts`) proves, against a real Pi 1.1.0
`AgentSession` with a scripted `pi-ai` faux model and no network:

1. Trusted approval, one mocked create, the saved run ID returned while the job is
   pending, an intervening user turn, one completion notice delivered at a settled
   boundary and acknowledged by its `custom_message` entry; terminal facts were
   persisted before the notice was scheduled.
2. Headless (`hasUI=false`): `APPROVAL_UNAVAILABLE`, zero creates.
3. Declined dialog: `APPROVAL_NOT_GRANTED`, zero creates, proposal still open.
4. Superseded proposal: `PROPOSAL_STALE`, no dialog, zero creates.
5. Completion during an active response: notice appended after the streaming
   answer, then a report turn; repeated terminal observations yield one notice.
6. Aborting the chat turn: `agent_settled aborted=true`, no remote cancel, job
   still running, completion delivered later, still one create.
7. Transient GET errors back off with growing delays; exhausted errors pause with
   `TRANSIENT_EXHAUSTED` while the remote status stays `running` and no outcome or
   notice is fabricated; timers are released.
8. `401` → `AUTH` pause; lost run (`404`) → `NOT_FOUND` pause; no cancel.
9. Unacknowledged create → `SUBMISSION_UNKNOWN` with no run ID; the late genuine
   ID is saved on the original attempt with monitoring `LATE_ACKNOWLEDGEMENT`
   paused; still one create.
10. Disposed runtime: delivery throws the stale-context error, the notice stays
    pending with the error recorded; a different session discovers the foreign
    notice and does not deliver it.

The RPC test (`guided-prototype.rpc.test.ts`) repeats the happy path in a real
`pi --mode rpc` process: the client answers the forwarded `confirm`
(`timeout: 600000`), prompts while the job is pending, completes the job through
`/exa-proto complete run_1` (disposition `handled`), observes the appended
`custom_message` and report through `get_entries`, replaces the session with
`new_session` (second attempt's monitor → `paused:SHUTDOWN`), and sends
`cancelled: true` for a third dialog (`APPROVAL_NOT_GRANTED`, zero creates in the
replaced runtime).

Run the prototype interactively with your own model:

```bash
pi -e packages/pi-exa/__tests__/fixtures/guided-prototype/pi-entry.ts
# ask for research, approve the dialog, then: /exa-proto complete run_1
```

## Unsupported guarantees (explicit)

- No exactly-once completion notification across crashes. The host offers no
  delivery acknowledgement API and holds queued deliveries in memory.
- No delivery into a session other than the one the runtime serves. Detached
  origins keep pending notices for explicit resume.
- No notifications after Pi exits. Monitoring is an in-process feature.
- No distinction between decline, dismissal and timeout of the approval dialog.
- No server retry guidance, create abort or idempotency from the Exa SDK.
- No evidence about interactive TUI rendering of the dialog or notice; that is
  the #175 interactive smoke.

## Consequences for the implementation contract

The settled public actions, consent binding, time bounds, cadence/backoff and
pause limits derived from this evidence are recorded in the architecture plan
section "#171 settled implementation contract". The qualification map carries a
#171 evidence row pointing at the two experiments.

section='''## #171 settled implementation contract

Evidence: [Pi host capability research](../research/2026-10-12-pi-guided-background-host-capabilities.md)
against Pi 1.1.0 (workspace pin moved from 1.0.3) and the runnable prototype in
`packages/pi-exa/__tests__/fixtures/guided-prototype/`. These decisions close the
four design gates above for #172–#175; they are implementation contract, not
prototype approval or spending authority. Material deviation requires operator review.

### Public actions

Keep the four planner names and the existing paid tools; add literals, not tools.

- `exa_research_summary mode="proposal"`: compile the current revision through the
  existing artifact compiler and render the readable proposal (question, scope and
  exclusions, criteria, carried assumptions, source strategy and selected context,
  deliverable, effort, providers/contact scope, processing/exclusion/continuation
  records, estimate and basis, lifetime allowance, existing liabilities, material
  uncertainty, and what is not a vendor cap). Return a `proposalId` bound to the
  artifact hash, plan revision and assessment basis. Non-spending; a newer proposal
  supersedes older unconsumed ones.
- `web_research_exa researchMode="submit"` with `cycleId` and `proposalId`: the only
  guided submission path. Inside the tool: recheck the proposal is current and
  unconsumed; if `ctx.hasUI` is false return `APPROVAL_UNAVAILABLE` and pause; call
  `ctx.ui.confirm` with the proposal text and the approval timeout; on `true` issue
  the lifetime scope and exact-request grants bound to that proposal (reusing the
  existing grant records), freeze and reserve the attempt exactly as `reserveAgent`
  does today, perform one bounded create, publish the remote ID, register the
  monitor, and return `{ cycleId, attemptId, runId, remoteStatus, monitoring }`
  without waiting for a terminal state. Any other dialog result returns
  `APPROVAL_NOT_GRANTED` and submits nothing. Model-writable parameters never carry
  consent; the grant is written only on the `true` branch of the host dialog.
- `exa_research_status` adds `monitor` (state, reason, gets, next delay, last
  success) and `notices` (pending / sent / acknowledged, acknowledged entry ID) to
  its view; `action="resume"` additionally restarts an eligible paused monitor for
  an acquired cycle (#174). Status never spawns a competing monitor.
- Existing `researchMode="active"` keeps the foundation's blocking contract for
  compatibility with already opted-in callers; tool guidance routes guided requests
  to `submit`. `recover`, `retry`, `replace`, standalone, default-opt-out and MCP
  behavior are unchanged. `recover` remains one bounded GET and shares the monitor's
  observation coordination so it cannot overlap a running check.

### Consent binding

`proposalId = hash(artifactHash, revision, assessmentBasis)`. The dialog body is the
rendered proposal; the operator never copies the hash. A plan edit changes the
artifact hash and therefore supersedes the proposal: approval of a superseded or
consumed proposal fails with `PROPOSAL_STALE` before any dialog or create. Decline,
dismissal, timeout and headless invocation are indistinguishable "not granted"
results; none is a consent event and none consumes the proposal.

### Submission and observation bounds

| Bound | Value | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| Create acknowledgement wait | 30 s | Separates acknowledgement from the 180 s full-run default; Exa creates return an ID in seconds. Expiry leaves the attempt `unknown`; a genuine late ID settles the original attempt with monitoring paused (`LATE_ACKNOWLEDGEMENT`). |
| Per-GET deadline | 15 s | One bounded request; deadlines never hold storage locks. |
| First check after acknowledgement | 5 s | Agent runs rarely finish sooner; avoids an immediate wasted GET. |
| Backoff | ×1.5 per pending observation or transient failure, capped at 60 s, ±20 % jitter, non-overlapping (the next check is scheduled only after the previous one completes) | Keeps long runs cheap while bounding notification latency to about one minute. |
| Transient failures | pause after 8 consecutive failures or 10 min without a successful GET | `ExaError` exposes no retry guidance, so local limits apply. |
| Auth (401/403) and not-found (404) | pause immediately (`AUTH`, `NOT_FOUND`) | Not proof of remote failure; remote outcome and liability stay separate. |
| Monitor lifetime | pause after 3 h (`MONITOR_LIFETIME`) | Exa publishes no maximum duration; explicit resume restarts observation without create. |
| Approval dialog timeout | 10 min | Expiry grants nothing. |

Monitoring has no create, continuation, retry, replacement or cancel authority.
Interrupting a chat turn aborts only the model turn: the saved run and its
liability continue; no cancel request is issued.

### Completion delivery protocol

1. On a terminal observation persist remote status, stop reason, classified usage
   and the local processing outcome on the attempt.
2. Persist one notice per attempt/terminal outcome with state `pending`. Repeated
   terminal observations of the same attempt create no second notice.
3. Deliver with `pi.sendMessage({ customType: "exa-research-completion", content:
   <attempt reference and read-only instruction>, display: true, details:
   { noticeId, cycleId, attemptId, runId, status } }, { triggerTurn: true,
   deliverAs: "followUp" })`. Idle origin → wakes now; streaming origin → after
   pending work; never `steer`. Content is a reference, never vendor output.
   Mark the notice `sent`.
4. Acknowledge by observation: on `agent_settled` or `session_start`, find the
   `custom_message` entry carrying `details.noticeId` in the session and mark the
   notice `acknowledged` with the entry ID. A `sent` notice without an entry after
   restart is `uncertain` and is reconciled, not re-sent automatically and not
   dropped. Exactly-once is not claimed.
5. A stale runtime (session replacement, reload, SDK dispose) throws on
   `sendMessage`; keep the notice `pending`, record the error, and let the origin
   session's `session_start` discovery surface it. Foreign sessions report but
   never deliver another session's notice.

### Lifecycle fences

Stop timers and mark monitors `paused:SHUTDOWN` on `session_shutdown` for every
reason; `session_start` marks any monitor left `registered`/`running` as
`paused:RESTART` and reports pending notices without delivering them. Explicit
resume (#174) reacquires ownership and restarts eligible monitors. Archive stops
monitoring and delivery and warns that remote work may continue.

### State dimensions

Keep four independent dimensions on each attempt: local submission
(`submitting`/`acknowledged`/`unknown`), remote lifecycle (`queued`/`running`/
`completed`/`failed`/`cancelled` plus stop reason), monitoring (`none`/
`registered`/`running`/`paused:<reason>`/`stopped`) and delivery
(`pending`/`sent`/`acknowledged`/`uncertain`). A paused monitor is not a failed
run; a sent notice is not a delivered one.

'''

#171 is done on `pi-exa-guided/prototype`: five commits, nothing pushed, all workspace checks green (lint, typecheck, 1037 tests, dependency audit). The upstack branches were rebased onto it.

**Commits**
- `chore(deps)`: Pi SDK moved from 1.0.3 to 1.1.0 across the workspace, per your instruction to target the latest 1.x.
- `test(pi-exa)`: runnable prototype under `packages/pi-exa/__tests__/fixtures/guided-prototype/` plus two experiments.
- `docs(pi-exa)`: Pi 1.1.0 host capability evidence at `docs/research/2026-10-12-pi-guided-background-host-capabilities.md`.
- `docs(pi-exa)`: settled implementation contract section in the architecture plan, a #171 evidence row in the qualification map, and an unreleased changelog note.
- `docs(pi-exa)`: result-inspection surfaces named and the active-mode decision flagged.

**Evidence produced**
- SDK experiment, ten scenarios against a real Pi session with a scripted model: trusted approval, headless fail-closed, decline, stale proposal, completion during an active response, abort without remote cancel, transient and auth and not-found pauses, unknown create with a late ID, stale-runtime delivery fence.
- RPC experiment, a real `pi --mode rpc` child process: the client answers the forwarded confirm dialog, prompts while the job is pending, completes the job via the extension command, verifies the persisted notice through `get_entries`, replaces the session, and refuses a cancelled dialog.
- Both are fully mocked. Zero paid calls, zero cancel requests, one create per approval.

**Capability verdicts that shape #172 to #174**
- Approval exists only through `ctx.ui.confirm` inside the submitting tool. Headless modes return false, so check `hasUI` first and fail closed.
- No delivery acknowledgement API. Acknowledge by finding the appended `custom_message` entry in the session; queued deliveries are in memory, so exactly-once is not claimable.
- A replaced or disposed runtime throws on `sendMessage`; the notice must stay pending for the origin session. Cross-session delivery is unsupported by design.
- The Exa SDK exposes no retry guidance, so backoff is local.

**Settled bounds**

| Bound | Value |
|---|---|
| Create acknowledgement wait | 30 s |
| Per-GET deadline | 15 s |
| First check, backoff, cap | 5 s, ×1.5, 60 s with ±20% jitter |
| Transient pause | 8 consecutive failures or 10 min silence |
| Monitor lifetime | 3 h |
| Approval dialog timeout | 10 min |

**One decision for you.** The contract keeps `researchMode=active` as the foundation's blocking path for already opted-in callers and routes guided requests to the new `submit`. PRD-010 v1.3 says the redesign replaces blocking cycle execution, so #172 could instead hide `active` behind `submit`. The plan flags this as pending your review.

**Not done**
- No interactive TUI run. The command `pi -e packages/pi-exa/__tests__/fixtures/guided-prototype/pi-entry.ts` is documented, but I exercised the RPC process, not a terminal. The interactive smoke remains the #175 gate.
- No push, no PRs, and the version-bump stash is untouched. Run or ask for `gh stack submit --auto` when you want the draft PR opened.

## Pi cycle branch

When Pi's `--exa-enable-cycles` integration is enabled, first read the
[durable cycle workflow](../../README.md#opt-in-durable-pi-planning).
Use that branch instead of the standalone fast path/payload defaults below:

1. Inspect status; obtain explicit start or resume for the intended cycle.
2. Clarify and record goal, scope, criteria, gaps and a draft-07 task contract.
3. Pause at permission instructions until the operator records the named
   lifetime scope/ceiling and any exact-request uncertainty assessment.
4. Attribute exploratory calls to the cycle, then explicitly curate candidates
   or external sources. Selected evidence is query context, not processing rows.
5. Preview the authoritative artifact; resolve conflicts by editing the plan,
   and obtain the operator's exact Agent request assessment before submission.
6. After success, use `exa_research_summary` with `mode: "brief"` or
   `"source_pack"` for findings, recorded gaps, assumptions and classified usage.
   Assess evidence yourself: generated claims/JSON and remote success do not
   satisfy criteria or verify billing.
7. Stop after success. Missing results use explicit same-run recovery; confirmed
   failure/unknown work uses only the documented explicitly funded retry/
   replacement policy. Further research after success needs a new cycle and
   operator permission. Paper retrieval belongs before completion; remaining
   paper gaps are reported, not autonomously fetched afterward.

A prose request, readiness or assistant-provided flags/amounts is not cycle
spending permission. This branch leaves standalone/default-opt-out/MCP behavior
unchanged. The remaining sections describe the standalone workflow.

----README 130-200
## Tools

### Opt-in durable Pi planning

Start Pi with `--exa-enable-cycles` to use durable research planning:

- `/exa-research start <topic>` creates an isolated cycle without paid work.
- `/exa-research list` lists readable saved cycles and coarse unreadable cycle IDs
  in this project. Unreadable contents are never displayed; attribution checks
  remain fail-closed until those records are repaired.
- `/exa-research resume <cycle-id>` explicitly acquires ownership after restart.
- `/exa-research approve <cycle-id> <total-dollar-ceiling> [tool,tool...]` records an operator
  grant for supported exploratory retrieval. Each approval sets the cycle's
  **total lifetime ceiling**, not additional credits. Grant history survives
  resume/archive; assistant approval fields do not establish consent.
  The optional comma-separated scope replaces the whole allowlist. Default scope:
  `web_search_exa`, `web_fetch_exa`, `web_find_similar_exa`, `web_search_advanced_exa`.
  `web_answer_exa` and `web_research_exa` require explicit scope amendments.
  Agent additionally requires the exact-request assessment below; including it
  in the lifetime scope alone never authorizes a submission or Connect/contact work.
- `/exa-research approve-request <cycle-id> <request-hash> <assessed-dollars>`
  approves one attempt of that exact uncertain request, after inspecting the
  denied tool call's request and SHA-256 hash. Changed arguments require new permission.
  Repeating/amending approval uses the latest record, never reviving older unused grants.
- `/exa-research approve-liability <cycle-id> <operation-id> <assessed-dollars>`
  names one existing unknown operation and an assessed allowance. It stays unknown,
  counts against the total ceiling, and never covers another unknown operation.
  Conflicting API receipts cannot be resolved through uncertainty permission.
- `/exa-research archive [cycle-id]` detaches and archives without deleting history.

The four `exa_research_*` tools then update, inspect, summarize, and archive the
active cycle. Reset does not cancel remote work or clear liabilities.
Session switches, forks, tree navigation, reload/shutdown detach the active cycle;
detachment fences pending start/resume operations too. Restart never automatically
resumes it. Live owners prevent competing resumes.
Related Git worktrees share a project namespace, not active session ownership.
Inherited Git repository/discovery environment overrides do not change that identity.

Curated JSON lives under the configured Pi agent directory's
`research-cycles/<project-id>/`, outside git, with private permissions.
Short transaction locks publish complete private PID/token records atomically.
Only proven-dead process owners are reclaimed; live processes are never evicted
by age. Competing reclaimers serialize, including bounded crashed-reclaimer
recovery. Legacy empty, malformed or unverifiable locks are retained: the error
names the lock path for explicit offline repair after confirming no process is
using the store. Never remove a live process lock or delete cycle history.
Storage hierarchy synchronization runs once per controller; private directory
ownership/type checks and record publication synchronization remain enforced.
Per-step raw notes/update payloads are not retained; selected source notes,
criteria, assumptions, gaps and revision metadata are retained.
Credentials and full raw retrieval archives are not written by this planner.
Invalid IDs/counters and unsupported records fail closed; restored evidence and
inspection diagnostics are recomputed from retained facts.
Unknown execution remains unknown after
resume; completed records cannot be edited back into executable planning.

The opted-in implementation includes durable planning, request compilation,
exploratory accounting, compiled Agent execution, explicit recovery and funded
retry/replacement. Attributed retrieval requires a recorded operator grant and an
atomic pre-call assessment. Include the active `cycleId` (and optionally
`expectedRevision`) on each exploratory tool call:

```json
{ "query": "Exa pricing", "researchMode": "active", "cycleId": "<active-cycle-id>", "expectedRevision": 0 }
```

Each operation reserves allowance before SDK invocation; concurrent calls share
pending estimates. Responses/status show API-reported totals, pending estimates,
unresolved operation IDs, operator-assessed liabilities and overspend separately.
Permission is rounded down, costs up, using safe integer micro-USD.
Only a genuine explicit SDK total (including zero) replaces its reservation.
----README 305-330
#### Compiled Agent attempts

With cycles enabled, an active `web_research_exa` call executes the exact current
artifact after **both** operator permissions:

1. `/exa-research approve <cycle-id> <total-dollar-ceiling> web_research_exa`
   explicitly includes Agent in the lifetime tool scope (include other desired
   tools in the comma-separated scope; amendments replace the scope/ceiling).
2. `/exa-research approve-request <cycle-id> <request-hash> <assessed-dollars>`
   names the full immutable request displayed by the permission pause, including
   effort, providers, continuation and contact-capable query/output contract.

The request hash is distinct from the preview artifact hash. Request permission
is single-use; plan changes require a new exact-request assessment. An assessment
below the published fixed-effort base price fails closed. Contact/Connect extras
and metered work need the explicit full-request assessment; neither the estimate
nor the cycle ceiling is a vendor-enforced billing cap. Generic exploratory
grants still exclude Agent. No assistant-supplied flags or numbers grant consent.

Before create, the controller atomically freezes the artifact, permission/budget
assessment and unique attempt/operation, persists intent, and claims one SDK
dispatch capability. Write/sync failure prevents submission. Progress includes
the remote ID as it becomes available; queued/running costs are provisional,
not final receipts. Terminal explicit totals (including zero) reconcile once.
Missing/malformed costs and local interruption remain unknown, not free work.

## Summary

Second layer of the pi-exa 6.1.0 stack (#172, stacked on #176): guide research from a conversational request through trusted approval to one acknowledged Exa submission, stopping at durable acknowledgement. Background monitoring and completion notification are #173.

**Package:** `@feniix/pi-exa` (opted-in Pi cycle path only; standalone, default-opt-out and MCP behavior unchanged).

## Changes

- `feat(pi-exa)`: record trusted-dialog approvals as one durable grant write. Grant/permission `source` widened to `command | dialog`; `grantDialogApproval` asserts the proposal's cycle, revision and artifact hash and writes the lifetime scope/ceiling plus the one-use exact-request permission in a single transaction.
- `feat(pi-exa)`: guided actions on the existing tools:
  - `exa_research_status action=start topic=…` creates a non-spending cycle conversationally.
  - `exa_research_summary mode=proposal` renders the readable scope/cost proposal (question, scope/exclusions, criteria, assumptions, source strategy, deliverable, effort, providers, rows, estimate and basis, lifetime allowance, existing liabilities) and a `proposalId` bound to the exact artifact hash, revision and estimate basis.
  - `web_research_exa researchMode=submit` with `cycleId` and `proposalId`: recomputes the proposal (`PROPOSAL_STALE` on mismatch), fails closed without a trusted UI (`APPROVAL_UNAVAILABLE`), asks through `ctx.ui.confirm` with the settled 10-minute timeout, and only on a real `true` records the grants, freezes the attempt, performs one bounded create through the new submit-only lifecycle (`submitResearchRun`: no polling, no cancel) and returns the saved run ID while the job is pending. Outcome is decided from the persisted attempt; silence closes the wait as `SUBMISSION_UNKNOWN` and a genuine late acknowledgement is saved on the original attempt without resubmission.
  - Exploratory retrieval without a covering grant is disclosed and approved through the same dialog (simple scope/ceiling cases only).
  - New `--exa-submit-timeout-ms` flag (default 30000).
- `docs(pi-exa)`: README guided section, planner skill Pi branch, CONCEPTS "Research proposal", changelog.

## Tests

`guided-submission.test.ts` runs the real registered extension against the private filesystem controller with a mocked Exa SDK: normal path (one create, zero GETs, zero cancels, run ID returned while pending, dialog-sourced grants persisted), stale proposal, declined/headless/forged approval, persistence failure before create, uncertain submission with late ID, exploratory dialog approval, guided setup failures that do not fall back to standalone, and metered effort without an estimate.

Run: `pnpm run check`, `pnpm run test` (1045 passed), `pnpm exec vitest run --coverage packages/pi-exa/__tests__`, `node scripts/check-release-changelog.mjs packages/pi-exa`. No paid calls.

## Honest limits

- The submit result labels monitoring as unavailable; the cycle sits at `running` until #173 adds the host-owned monitor.
- No interactive TUI run; the dialog was exercised through the registered-tool harness (#175 owns the interactive smoke).

## Decision requested

`researchMode=active` is retained as the foundation's blocking path for already opted-in callers; guided requests route to `submit`. PRD-010 v1.3 replaces blocking execution, so this could instead be hidden behind `submit`. Unchanged from #176; #173 can proceed either way.

Closes #172.

Outcome is decided from the persisted attempt; silence closes the wait as `SUBMISSION_UNKNOWN` and a genuine late acknowledgement is saved on the original attempt without resubmission.

failure after a create still returns the saved run ID with monitoring paused.

entry point, since the registration is installed during Pi's own session_start.
